messages:
raj: Thinking out loud — I sketched a lightweight proposal to reduce eviction-induced tail latency for small tenants. current problem: full-scan evictions during ramp cause CPU spikes and long stalls.

jessica: link to the sketch?

raj: pasted below. gist: move from monolithic eviction passes to tiny ad-hoc scans per demux key, rate-limited and idempotent. each scan only touches a prefix shard instead of the whole slab. benefits: smaller p99 impact, easier cancellation. downsides: can leave stale entries longer, harder to reason about fairness.

sam: curious how you handle correctness — what if two scans race on overlapping prefixes?

raj: plan: scans are scoped to exclusive prefix ranges by min/max token, acquired via fast-fence token. pseudo: ```
if (acquire_fence(prefix_range)) {
  do_scan_and_evict(prefix_range);
  release_fence(prefix_range);
} else {
  noop; // retry later
}
```

maria: fence token acquisition seems like a lease. how long do we hold it? if long -> blocks handlers, if short -> expensive churn.

raj: aim for short windows (50-200ms), only evict cold candidates. we don't block reads — fence only prevents concurrent scans. reads still consult per-key residency bits and may observe stale entries until eviction completes.

jin: how do we score eviction candidates? global LRU is expensive. we could use cheap heuristics: recent-hit flag + approximate recency (8-bit timestamp), and only when candidate score < threshold include in scan result.

jessica: also: need a fallback for strict correctness workloads (enterprise). maybe expose a tenant-level policy: "strong-clean" triggers synchronous compaction for that tenant when requested.

raj: yep — two-tier: default = best-effort ad-hoc scans; enterprise opt-in = sync compaction or privileged background worker that can take longer leases and do full passes.

sam: any telemetry needs? we should emit per-scan duration, bytes touched, evicts performed, and conflicts (fence misses). helps tune rate limits.

maria: +1 on metrics. also track "staleness window" per prefix so we can alert if entries are stuck too long.

raj: good. open questions: 1) demux granularity — fixed-size ranges vs. hash-aligned prefixes. 2) admission control for scan rate during global pressure. 3) how to test racey correctness (fuzzers?).

jin: for (1) prefer power-of-two buckets aligned with slab to avoid cross-slab touches. easier to reason about accounting.

jessica: for (2) tie scan tokens to current memory-pressure signal + tenant fairness weights. don't let one noisy tenant monopolize scan throughput.

sam: for (3) we can write a deterministic simulator + small fuzzer that perturbs lease timing and interleaves reads/writes; also integration test that validates read-after-write invariants under concurrent scans.

raj: I'll draft a tiny RFC with the proto for fence tokens, scan RPC, metrics, and a canary plan. aim to land spike in next sprint.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: raj/prototype/eviction-scanner -> staging at 2026-04-02T06:00:00Z :rocket:

maria: thanks, looking forward to the RFC. if you want me to pair on the simulator ping me.

raj: thanks — will ping. will include sample histograms for target p99 improvements.
